# Vendor comparison

Vendors A, B and C refer to the quotes in the order supplied. All figures use the supplied, unspecified currency. This comparison assumes equivalent scope and usage; taxes, implementation charges, overages and renewal increases have not been supplied.

## Recommendation

Prefer Vendor A provisionally, provided it covers the required regions and its integration effort does not erase the subscription savings. Vendor C is the alternative if its coverage or reduced integration work justifies an additional 15k per year. Vendor B needs the strongest justification: it has the highest annual price and requires a two-year commitment. No final selection is supported until the technical differences are mapped to the individual vendors.

## Price and commitment

| Vendor | Annual quote | Two-year subscription cost at unchanged rates | Commitment supplied | Annual premium over A |
| --- | ---: | ---: | --- | ---: |
| A | 40k | 80k | Not specified | — |
| B | 62k | 124k | Two years | 22k (55%) |
| C | 55k | 110k | Not specified | 15k (37.5%) |

B's quoted two-year commitment implies 124k in subscription fees, assuming the annual figure applies in both years. This does not imply upfront payment. A's and C's two-year figures are comparison scenarios, not confirmed commitments or guaranteed renewal prices. Their cancellation and renewal terms remain unknown.

Over two years, B costs 44k more than A and 14k more than C. C costs 30k more than A. B's longer commitment also reduces the opportunity to switch if requirements or service quality change; termination rights have not been supplied.

## Coverage

The existing evaluation says regional coverage differs. It does not identify each vendor's supported regions or the mandatory regions for this project. Required coverage is a selection gate: a lower quote does not compensate for missing a required region.

## Latency

All three meet the latency bar according to the first evaluation round. There is no recorded evidence of a latency advantage that would justify a premium.

## Integration effort

One vendor requires substantially more integration work, but the existing notes do not identify it. Compare implementation, maintenance and operating effort over the same evaluation horizon. If A is the more demanding option, C's extra subscription spend breaks even only if C avoids at least 30k of other costs over two years, assuming unchanged rates. B would need at least 44k of equivalent benefit relative to A, or 14k relative to C, before accounting for the commitment's loss of flexibility. Benefits may also include necessary coverage or capabilities rather than direct cost savings.

## Before final selection

- Map each quote to its vendor, regional coverage and integration estimate.
- Confirm the quoted tier supports the expected workload; this remains an open question in the project notes.
- Confirm comparable inclusions, implementation charges, usage limits, overages, renewal prices and termination terms.
- Allow approximately ten working days for legal review, as recorded in the project notes.

The recommendation is provisional and does not authorize a purchase.
